findings.title: Authentication state is inferred from human-readable error text
findings.evidence: app/page.tsx derives authenticationRequired with loadError.includes("Sign in"); features/workspace/api.ts throws only an Error string and discards the HTTP status. The same substring test also selects the sign-in action in the error banner.
findings.impact: Changing server wording or returning an unrelated error containing that phrase can select the wrong workspace state. The UI and service are implicitly coupled through copy rather than a stable contract.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the response status on a small API error type and use status 401 to select the sign-in state; keep messages for display.

findings.title: Mutation refresh failures are hidden from action callers
findings.evidence: features/workspace/use-workspace.ts catches link load errors inside load() and refresh() resolves after load(); features/links/use-link-actions.ts awaits refresh() then reports creation, pause, resume or deletion success.
findings.impact: When the write succeeds but reloading fails, the action reports success while the displayed links may be stale. A load error is shown separately, but the action has no contract for distinguishing a completed refresh from a failed one.
findings.recommendation: Return an explicit refresh result, or otherwise communicate that the write succeeded but the list could not be refreshed; retain the separate analytics and health loading behavior.
